slides.texte_overlay:
How to become the calmest
guy in any room
Expect small things to go wrong. The train will be late, the coffee will spill. When you expect bumps, they stop shocking you, and you stay steady while others panic.
Speak last in a heated discussion. Let everyone else get their emotions out first. The calm voice at the end is usually the one people listen to most.
Don't take things personally. A rude driver, a short reply, a bad mood at work. Most of it is about their day, not about you. Letting it go keeps you calm.
Give your mind a quiet place to go. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and it's become my reset button whenever things get loud and stressful.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. It's become my reset button whenever things get loud and stressful.

slides.texte_overlay: Train your body hard a few times a week. A tired body after a good workout leaves little energy for anxiety. Physical calm turns into mental calm.
Cut caffeine after lunch. Too much coffee looks a lot like anxiety: fast heart, quick words, restless hands. Your afternoon self will be noticeably calmer.
Prepare for the hard moments before they happen. A difficult meeting, a tough conversation. Thinking it through the night before means you walk in already calm.
